summary: Astrid makes clear that knowing New York well has not required becoming less Norse or less herself.

panelPlan.action: Astrid thinks; this is not a slogan setup.
Carrie and Bjorn both look at her.

dialogueInline.text: Do you feel that living here has changed who you are?
Yes.
I know this city now. I know things I did not know. I still know my people. I still know where I came from.
I didn't ask you to give that up.
Good.

directionInline.text: Astrid remains visibly Norse and herself; do not stage the exchange as a transformation or assimilation victory.

summary: Asked for the household's collective intention, Bjorn answers only for himself and protects everyone else's right to have already answered differently.

panelPlan.action: Bjorn's posture changes; this is the question he once would have seized.
Hearing Officer waits for the collective answer.
Bjorn looks briefly at the other four applicants.

dialogueInline.text: You have described yourself as responsible for this household. Does the household intend permanent residence?
I intend to remain.
They have answered for themselves.

summary: Bjorn defines leadership after necessity: responsibility means offering strength and judgment without claiming ownership of another person's future.

panelPlan.action: Bjorn looks down at his armored forearm, then at the household.

dialogueInline.text: If they no longer require your decisions, what is your role?
I carry when I am asked.
I give judgment when it is wanted.
I stand when someone needs a hand beside them.
Strength does not make another person's road mine.

summary: Carrie refuses to turn integration into one score and gives the hearing authority the narrower facts actually needed to judge whether these adults can live here.

panelPlan.action: Carrie looks at the file, then closes it.

dialogueInline.text: Ms. Carrie, are these applicants integrated?
They can maintain housing. They use the city. They meet obligations. They form relationships I didn't assign.
They know when to ask for help. They also know when not to ask me.
That wasn't exactly my question.
It's the answer I can support.

summary: The hearing authority grants the five applicants permanent temporal-resident status individually, preserving the household without making it a legal requirement that they remain one unit forever.

panelPlan.action: Wide. The Hearing Officer reviews a final page, marks the file, and speaks in ordinary administrative cadence rather than delivering a speech.
Reaction strip across five applicants and Carrie. No cheering. Each absorbs a different meaning.
Hearing Officer, already moving to the next document.

dialogueInline.text: The record supports permanent temporal-resident status for each of the five applicants, individually.
The Bushwick placement may continue under ordinary tenancy and program rules. Intensive DTI case supervision is no longer required as a condition of residence.
We may remain.
Yes.
And nothing in this order requires all five of you to make the same future choice.

directionInline.text: Deliver the ruling in ordinary administrative cadence. No cheering, gavel spectacle, or triumphal courtroom staging.

summary: Outside the hearing room, the household begins processing the ruling, but Astrid simply returns to the ordinary independent life the hearing finally made visible.

dialogueInline.text: Okay. The order still has to get entered, housing gets a copy, DTI will—
Where are you going?
Home later.

directionInline.text: No narration or victory caption. Astrid leaves independently and merges into ordinary city pedestrian traffic.
